title: Idempotency and nullable context invariants for ParamType.convert
answers: What invariants must custom ParamType subclasses satisfy in Click?
Why does ParamType.convert receive None for ctx or param?
How should validation errors be raised inside ParamType.convert?
body:
`src/click/types.py:ParamType.convert` must be idempotent: if `value` is already of the expected target type (e.g. from pre-converted defaults or chained converters), return it immediately without re-processing.
Implementations must handle `ctx=None` and `param=None` safely because prompts (`src/click/termui.py:prompt`) and direct invocations call `convert()` outside a running command context.
Never raise raw `ValueError` or `TypeError` directly; always call `self.fail(message, param, ctx)` so Click can attach parameter metadata and raise `src/click/exceptions.py:BadParameter`. Skipping `fail()` causes uncaught exceptions and bypasses CLI error formatting.
says: Entering invalid input at an interactive prompt crashes instead of showing friendly guidance.
Custom input validation shows an unhandled crash rather than a clean error message.
Prevent default values from being validated and converted multiple times during execution.
Interactive console questions crash when user validation logic runs without active environment.
Format validation errors neatly on the command line instead of dumping crash logs.
